item.text:
Research continuation completed across all eight chapters. No scores or ranking advice were assigned.

Local persistence remains blocked: the sandbox rejects repository commands before execution. Parent persistence is required.

### New defensible ledger units

- **E058 — IAEA safeguards and non-diversion.** IAEA GOV/INF/2023/11, pp. 1–2, paras. 4–10: Brazil stated naval-propulsion material would not be used for nuclear weapons; fuel-cycle facilities were under IAEA/ABACC safeguards; consultations addressed sensitive facilities and verification design. Maps 1B.1–1B.4. [IAEA report](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/documents/govinf2023-11.pdf)

- **E059 — Ongoing 2023 safeguards process.** Same report, p. 3, paras. 11–14: consultations remained ongoing; the IAEA received preliminary information on planned facilities from Brazil via ABACC on 25 May 2023. Maps 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.6, 8B.2. [IAEA report](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/documents/govinf2023-11.pdf)

- **E060 — National cybersecurity policy.** Decree 11.856/2023, arts. 1–7: Lula signed Brazil’s first dedicated national cybersecurity policy, including critical-infrastructure resilience, risk management, fundamental-rights protections, international cooperation, and a multi-sector cybersecurity committee. Maps 1B.6, 1B.8, 8B.2, 8B.6. [Presidential decree](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2023/decreto/D11856.htm)

- **E061 — Refusal of weapons transfers to Ukraine.** Carnegie, paras. 90–99: Lula stated Brazil would not send weapons or ammunition to Ukraine and pursued a neutral mediation initiative. Maps 2B.1, 2B.3, 2B.7, 2B.8. [Carnegie](https://carnegieendowment.org/research/2023/12/brazil-in-the-emerging-world-order?center=china&lang=en)

- **E062 — Mixed Ukraine posture.** Carnegie, paras. 91–95: Brazil opposed Russia’s invasion in multiple UN votes and supported withdrawal of Russian troops, but abstained on suspending Russia from the Human Rights Council and declined the U.S.-led coalition. Maps 2B.3, 2B.6, 2B.7. Contrary evidence: neutrality weakened accountability according to the analysis. [Carnegie](https://carnegieendowment.org/research/2023/12/brazil-in-the-emerging-world-order?center=china&lang=en)

- **E063 — Gaza ceasefire diplomacy.** Carnegie, paras. 85–86: Brazil led a UN Security Council ceasefire effort in October 2023; the proposal was vetoed by the United States. Maps 2B.6, 2B.7, 2B.10. [Carnegie](https://carnegieendowment.org/research/2023/12/brazil-in-the-emerging-world-order?center=china&lang=en)

- **E064 — Federal intervention after 8 January.** Ministry of Justice report: Lula’s Decree 11.377 authorized a 23-day federal intervention, removed or suspended Brasília security officials, and initiated military-police inquiries. Maps 3B.4, 3B.9, 3B.10, 4B.4, 4B.10, 8B.3, 8B.5. [Justice Ministry](https://www.gov.br/mj/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/intervencao-federal-na-seguranca-do-df-e-concluida-apos-23-dias-de-vigencia/)

- **E065 — Operation Lesa Pátria.** Federal Police, March 2023: searches and preventive arrests targeted participants, financiers, omissions, and inciters connected to the January 8 attack. Maps 3B.9, 4B.4, 4B.10, 7B.6, 8B.5. [Federal Police](https://www.gov.br/pf/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/2023/03/pf-deflagra-8a-fase-da-operacao-lesa-patria-para-identificar-participantes-dos-ataques-do-dia-8-1/)

- **E066 — Continuing police-abuse contrary evidence.** U.S. State Department 2023 report, paras. 37–44: unlawful killings and police violence remained significant; Rio recorded 651 deaths linked to police incidents through July, though below the prior year. Maps 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.5, 3B.10. [State Department report](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2107626.html)

- **E067 — Civil-liberty conditions.** Same report, paras. 121–135: expression, media, assembly, and association were generally protected; reported censorship, online threats, criminal-defamation rules, and election-related content restrictions remained contrary evidence. Maps 4B.3, 4B.5, 4B.6, 4B.8, 4B.10. [State Department report](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2107626.html)

- **E068 — 2023 labor outcomes.** IBGE: unemployment was 7.8%; employment reached 100.7 million; formal employment reached 37.7 million; real earnings rose 7.2%; informality remained substantial. Maps 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.10, 8B.7. Existing prior E051 should be reconciled with this unit rather than duplicated.

- **E069 — Poverty reduction and inequality.** IBGE reports poverty falling from 31.6% to 27.4% between 2022 and 2023, with 8.7 million fewer people below the poverty line; racial, gender, regional, and labor-market disparities persisted. Maps 5B.6, 5B.10, 6B.9, 6B.10, 8B.7. [IBGE](https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/en/agencia-news/2184-news-agency/news/42113-in-2023-poverty-in-the-country-drops-to-lowest-level-since-2012)

- **E070 — Regional income disparities.** IBGE 2023 household-income release: national per-capita income was R$1,893, compared with R$1,155 in the Northeast, R$1,314 in the North, and R$2,264 in the Central-West. Maps 5B.6, 5B.7, 5B.10, 6B.9, 8B.7.

- **E071 — Mais Médicos implementation.** Ministry of Health: six months after relaunch, 18,500 doctors served more than 4,000 municipalities, with emphasis on poorer and underserved areas. Maps 5B.6, 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.8, 6B.9, 8B.2, 8B.6. [Ministry of Health](https://www.gov.br/saude/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/2023/setembro/com-mais-de-18-5-mil-profissionais-mais-medicos-bate-recorde-historico-seis-meses-apos-a-retomada-do-programa)

- **E072 — Mais Médicos statutory expansion.** Lula sanctioned the 2023 law creating 15,000 new vacancies; the Ministry reported 3,620 selected doctors already active and serving over 20.5 million people. Maps 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.8, 8B.1, 8B.2. [Ministry of Health](https://www.gov.br/saude/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/2023/julho/presidente-lula-sanciona-lei-do-mais-medicos-com-criacao-de-15-mil-novas-vagas-em-2023/)

- **E073 — Bolsa Família reach.** By November 2023, Bolsa Família covered 21.18 million families in all 5,570 municipalities; federal transfers reached R$155.37 billion in the first eleven months. Maps 5B.1, 5B.6, 6B.1, 6B.9, 8B.1, 8B.2. [Brazilian government](https://www.gov.br/secom/pt-br/acompanhe-a-secom/noticias/2023/11/bolsa-familia-chega-a-21-18-milhoes-de-familias-a-partir-desta-sexta-17)

- **E074 — CGU anti-corruption and audit capacity.** CGU 2023 management report, pp. 6–7: 192 investigations, 281 policy/contract evaluations, 203 preventive tender audits, 36 special operations, and 40 expulsive sanctions. Maps 7B.6, 7B.9, 8B.2, 8B.5. [CGU report](https://repositorio.cgu.gov.br/bitstream/1/78263/1/Relatorio_de_Gest%C3%A3o_2023.pdf)

- **E075 — CGU transparency reversal.** CGU report, pp. 70–72: 252 secrecy cases were reviewed; 178 prior decisions were modified; 2,067 access-to-information appeals were decided, with 57% favoring or partially favoring requesters. Maps 4B.6, 4B.10, 7B.6, 7B.9, 8B.2, 8B.5. [CGU report](https://repositorio.cgu.gov.br/bitstream/1/78263/1/Relatorio_de_Gest%C3%A3o_2023.pdf)

- **E076 — CGU institutional restructuring.** CGU report, pp. 9, 69–70: Decree 11.529/2023 created a federal integrity/transparency/access-to-information system, and Decree 11.330/2023 created a National Access to Information Secretariat. Administration-level evidence only; not proof of Lula’s personal honesty. Maps 7B.6, 7B.9, 8B.2, 8B.5.

### Chapter handoff

**1B:** Recovered precise IAEA safeguards and non-diversion evidence plus the national cybersecurity decree. Remaining gaps are biological-risk governance, command-and-control implementation audits, AI outcomes, and catastrophic-risk crisis decisions.

**2B:** Added a clear restraint/non-transfer record, UN voting behavior, mediation efforts, and Gaza diplomacy. Contrary evidence is Brazil’s neutrality and limited accountability pressure. No Brazilian 2023 foreign military operation, proxy conduct, or military-accountability proceeding was recovered.

**3B:** Added direct federal intervention and Lesa Pátria evidence. These support authority, investigation, and remedy. State-level police killings and prison conditions remain only partly attributable.

**4B:** Added balanced State Department evidence: generally protected expression, assembly, association, and internet access alongside censorship reports and online restrictions. Direct opposition-treatment, surveillance, media-owner pressure, term-limit, and self-binding evidence remain incomplete.

**5B:** Added independent 2023 labor, poverty, and regional-income outcomes. Results improved materially, but informality and regional inequality persisted. Attribution remains shared with macroeconomic conditions, Congress, and central-bank autonomy.

**6B:** Added official poverty, income-distribution, Bolsa Família, and Mais Médicos evidence. Education, sanitation, housing quality, disability, and durable nationwide service-quality outcomes remain gaps.

**7B:** CGU evidence materially strengthens administration-level transparency, access-to-information, audit, and conflict-prevention claims. It does not establish Lula’s personal enrichment, honesty, family benefit, procurement conduct, or obstruction. Attribution remains high-risk.

**8B:** The portfolio now includes primary implementation evidence, independent labor and poverty outcomes, social-service reach, cybersecurity governance, democratic-crisis response, and integrity-system outputs. Durable cross-portfolio effectiveness remains unresolved.

### Manifest dispositions to persist

Append E058–E076 as `final_evidence` except where the existing ledger already contains the same atomic claim:

- Reconcile E051 with E068.
- Reconcile E054 with E071–E072.
- Reconcile E055–E057 with E074–E076.
- Upgrade E023 to `final_evidence` and replace its missing locator with IAEA pp. 1–3, paras. 4, 11–14.
- Keep E037 as `snippet_caveat` unless the Reuters body is independently opened.
- Retain E020 and E021 as explicit gaps, never as negative evidence.
- Preserve all chapter mappings and contrary-evidence fields.
- Do not create any score, range, ranking, anchor, or score/null recommendation.
